title: Instagram Unveils ‘More Modern’ New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It
description:
Meta’s Instagram proudly launched a new logo Thursday — its first update in a decade — and the trolling has already begun.

	“The wordmark at the to
body:
Meta’s Instagram proudly launched a new logo Thursday — its first update in a decade — and the trolling has already begun.

	“The wordmark at the top of the app hasn’t changed in 10 years, so it was time for a refresh,” Instagram head Adam Mosseri wrote in a post on the platform. “Cleaner and more modern, with references to the original and the simplicity and craft that’s always made it Instagram.”

	Instagram fans immediately latched on to the fact that the stylized “r” in the new logo could be easily confused with another letter, like “z” or “u.”
	

	“Is it just me or It reads : instagzam ❓,” one commenter said in reply to Mosseri’s big reveal. Another user commented, “Instagwam – how a toddler would pronounce it. Perfect.”

	Someone else quipped: “Instaguam! Nice to see the US territory finally getting its due.”

	The multihued Instagram icon, an abstract representation of a camera, isn’t changing. For the record, here is what the previous, cursive-y looking Instagram wordmark looks like:

schema.headline: Instagram Unveils ‘More Modern’ New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It

title: Shannon Elizabeth’s Long, Bumpy Road to OnlyFans Stardom
description:
Shannon Elizabeth is no stranger to breaking the internet.

	Following the release of 1999’s “American Pie,” the cumming-of-age film that launched E
body:
Shannon Elizabeth is no stranger to breaking the internet.

	Following the release of 1999’s “American Pie,” the cumming-of-age film that launched Elizabeth to stardom (and sex symbol status), she decided she needed a website.

	“I think I was one of the first actors to have one,” she recalls to Variety. “The only people who had websites at the time were porn stars. That was it. So, everyone thought, ‘Why are you putting a website up?’ But we thought that was the next step in the evolution of things.”
	

	Elizabeth, whose revealing turn as the Czech exchange student Nadia earned her a nomination for Breakthrough Female Performance at the MTV Movie Awards and several Maxim covers, attempted to host a live chat session with fans only to crash the site’s servers. And now, a quarter century later, the actress and animal rights activist throttled the internet once more by launching an OnlyFans in April, raking in millions during her first few months on the platform.


	“I crossed $1 million in nine days,” she shares. “It was really surprising, and I was honored that my fans came out and supported me. I had no idea what to expect, and the response has been really amazing. I’m chatting with people all the time and it’s been a lot of fun.”

	The “Scary Movie” star, 52, has joined a number of other renowned actors and musicians who have taken their talents to the paid-content site, such as Bella Thorne, Denise Richards, Cardi B, Iggy Azalea and “Sopranos” actress Drea de Matteo, who had only $10 in her bank account and used her OnlyFans earnings to prevent her house from going into foreclosure, later declaring, “OnlyFans saved my life.”
	

	“There are a bunch of actors that have recently gotten on and we’re starting to pull it back to what it was meant to be,” offers Elizabeth. “It doesn’t have to be only for adult entertainment. It can be whatever you want it to be.”

	There is also the case of 85-year-old “Knots Landing” star Donna Mills, who joined OnlyFans last month and has been making a killing. Both Mills and Elizabeth are being managed by Joseph D. Reitman, a journeyman actor and producer who also happens to be Elizabeth’s ex-husband.

	“Shannon has always been someone who genuinely enjoys connecting with and giving back to her fans, and this allows her to do that in a more direct, meaningful way than ever before. It’s a powerful model, and right now, there’s nothing more effective at facilitating that connection than OnlyFans,” Reitman told Variety.



	

					Jason Biggs, Shannon Elizabeth and Chris Klein in “American Pie.”
									©Universal/Courtesy Everett Collection
	



	OnlyFans was initially founded in 2016 as a Patreon-esque subscription service wherein celebrities would be paid directly by their fans in exchange for access, and it banned any and all explicit content. That ban was lifted in 2017; and by 2019, when cam site owner Leonid Radvinsky acquired a majority interest in the company, it had become primarily known as a destination for adult creators and pornographic content. The site exploded in popularity at the height of the Covid pandemic and the corresponding economic recession, growing from 20 million to 120 million users. Today, OnlyFans boasts over 400 million users worldwide as well as approximately 4 million content creators who’ve earned more than $25 billion since its inception. OnlyFans takes a 20% commission while its creators keep the remaining 80%.

	Like de Matteo, OnlyFans has helped Elizabeth dig herself out of a financial rut. She’d recently filed for divorce from her husband of five years, Simon Borchert; Hollywood residuals ain’t what they used to be; and the acting roles had dried up due to a mix of her primarily living in South Africa — where she runs her non-profit animal rescue organization Animal Avengers — and old-school Hollywood ageism. Elizabeth has always enjoyed visiting fan conventions like Comic-Con and interacting with her admirers, so it seemed like an extension of that.
	

	“I was going through a divorce here in South Africa and was chatting to my manager Joe about what’s next and how to restart things in my life. I had really neglected a lot of things, and he brought it up as an option. I wasn’t sure and didn’t know much about it, and we looked into it, and I thought, ‘Yeah, why not?’” explains Elizabeth.

	She continues, “For the last ten years I’ve been living off of my savings for the most part because I haven’t been as focused on work. To be able to get myself back to the point where I’m not struggling and am able to choose projects because I like them and not because I need the money — it’s definitely giving me more freedom to do that.”

	Animal Avengers was started as an L.A. dog and cat rescue in 2001, right after Elizabeth’s one-two punch of “American Pie” and “Scary Movie.” After observing a harrowing video of an elephant being poached in South Africa, she realized she “wanted to help animals on a bigger scale” and started exploring animal rights efforts in the country, eventually moving there in 2016. She was also appalled by photos of Donald Trump’s sons trophy hunting endangered animals that resurfaced during his first presidential campaign.

	“It’s horrific,” she says, adding, “And there’s a big difference between hunting to use all of the animal and feed your village versus trophy hunting, which usually involves endangered animals and they just want the trophy. To me, there’s a mental imbalance there to want to do that to an animal at all.”

	Currently, Animal Avengers supports anti-poaching efforts, including programs that help rangers buy supplies, tag animals, do rhino-horn trimmings (to inhibit their poaching) and has a sanctuary on a leased piece of land where they care for a blind black rhino named Manute. She says she’s looking to acquire their own piece of land in or around Cape Town to erect an animal rehabilitation center and wildlife hospital.



	

									Shannon Elizabeth
	



	And a good portion of Elizabeth’s OnlyFans earnings gets poured back into Animal Avengers.

	“So much of what I do goes back to the animals. There are a lot of expenses that go into it, and I don’t charge a salary for myself or charge travel I do for charity work to the charity. I’ll pay for that myself,” she maintains. “It allows me to cover admin expenses so that all of the charity’s money goes to animals in the field.”
	

	Elizabeth’s first foray into acting came during her senior year of high school in Waco, Texas, when she landed the role of a cheerleader extra in the music video for the 1990 song “I Just Can’t Handle It” by the local R&B group Hi-Five. That video was helmed by a little-known director by the name of Antoine Fuqua (the man behind the $1 billion-grossing Michael Jackson biopic “Michael”) and produced by Robert Goodman, who encouraged her to get into modeling, which she did nine days after graduating high school. She modeled in Japan, China and Taiwan, before venturing out to L.A. and booking a Sunkist commercial. Then she booked another commercial. She took acting classes, signed with a small agency and landed a small role on the HBO show “Arliss,” playing a Russian tennis player with an accent. Then came the low-budget horror film, “Jack Frost,” followed shortly thereafter by “American Pie.”  

	“American Pie,” which turns 25 this year, has experienced a cultural reassessment in recent years — particularly the sequence where Elizabeth’s character Nadia is broadcast online disrobing and pleasuring herself without her consent.

	“With the whole #MeToo movement, everyone is scared to say anything now or do anything, and comedy is always going to offend somebody, so it’s just a different day and age,” she reasons. “But I think it will all come back around at some point. People are yearning for connection. I love ‘American Pie.’ It meant a lot for my life and my career. I don’t go back and analyze it content-wise, and it made everything for me. I don’t have anything bad to say about it.”

	After the success of “American Pie,” which grossed over $235 million against an $11 million budget, Elizabeth signed a three-picture deal with Miramax, which put her in the crosshairs of notorious brothers Harvey and Bob Weinstein.

	“We did have some run-ins with Harvey, but my manager and my ex, Joe, were both very protective of me,” remembers Elizabeth. “So, when occasions arose that could have gone very wrong, they didn’t allow it to happen. If I was invited to meet Harvey somewhere, they would say no.”



	

					Regina Hall, Shannon Elizabeth and Anna Faris in “Scary Movie.”
									©Dimension Films/Everett Collection / Everett Collection
	



	Perhaps that — and a miscommunication over whether Elizabeth would pose in a men’s magazine to promote “Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back” — is why Elizabeth fell out of favor with Weinstein, a convicted rapist known for holding actresses’ careers hostage if they turned down his advances.
	

	“Harvey did threaten my career,” Elizabeth alleges, claiming he told her representation something to the effect of, “Lose my number. Don’t ever call me again about her or I’ll end her career.”

	Elizabeth’s three-picture deal with Miramax subsequently ended after only two films, and she also says that is the reason why she never returned for future entries in the “Scary Movie” franchise: “I think there’s a definite reason they didn’t [bring me back].”

	Whether due to Weinstein’s machinations or not, Elizabeth’s acting career began to lose steam not long after he turned on her. She dabbled in professional poker for a handful of years in the mid-aughts, mostly raising money for her non-profit, and was coached by poker legend Annie Duke — Reitman’s wife at the time, who’d also taught poker to Matt Damon and Ben Affleck — but “it wasn’t my calling.” Post-divorce, she says she’s ready to dive back into acting and producing, and even applied for a South African visa so she can work on film and television projects out there as well.

	“I’m signing on to produce a project and be in it, and we’re looking at a few others that are coming to us,” Elizabeth reveals. “It’s exciting to be back in the game, in that sense. And I really want to direct and be behind the camera.”

	In the meantime, she’s busy directing and producing her OnlyFans content, which does not currently contain any nudity, even though many of Elizabeth’s posts entice fans of hers to purchase images that appear to be nude, only to reveal her clothed:



	

	



	That may change, however.  

	“I’ve got to be a little bit mysterious,” she teases. “I do all kinds of content, but I don’t even know what my boundaries will be. I’m still exploring it and as I become more comfortable with it, I’m going to push those boundaries.”

schema.headline: Shannon Elizabeth’s Long, Bumpy Road to OnlyFans Stardom

title: Amy Sedaris Joins Ben Stiller, Benicio Del Toro in Apple TV Comedy ‘Protective Custody’
description:
Amy Sedaris is the latest addition to the Apple TV comedy series “Protective Custody,” Variety has learned. 

	Sedaris will star alongside previousl
body:
Amy Sedaris is the latest addition to the Apple TV comedy series “Protective Custody,” Variety has learned. 

	Sedaris will star alongside previously announced series lead Ben Stiller as well as fellow cast member Benicio Del Toro. 

	The logline for the show states that it will follow “a disgraced financier (Stiller) accused of massive fraud who is thrown into protective custody, where he must navigate prison politics, salvage his reputation, and confront the consequences of his actions while awaiting trial.” 
	

	Further character details are being kept under wraps. 

	Sedaris is perhaps best known for starring in the cult hit comedy “Strangers with Candy,” which she co-created. Her other TV credits include “At Home with Amy Sedaris” and “BoJack Horseman,” while she has also starred in films such as “Jennifer’s Body,” “Puss in Boots,” and “Elf.” She earned two Emmy nominations for “At Home with Amy Sedaris” in the Outstanding Variety Sketch Series category. She has also frequently collaborated with Jon Favreau, including on his films “Chef” and the live-action “Lion King,” as well as in his “Star Wars” shows “The Mandalorian” and “The Book of Boba Fett.” Next up, she will appear in Favreau’s Oswald the Lucky Rabbit series at Disney+. 

	She is repped by CAA and attorney James Adams. 

	Mike Judge is co-writing “Protective Custody” along with Steve Hely and Dave King. All three are executive producers and co-showrunners, with Judge also attached to direct. Stiller will executive produce in addition to starring via Red Hour. John Lesher of Red Hour also executive produces, as does Ben Silverman, Howard Owens, and Rodney Ferrell of Propagate Content. Michael Rotenberg and Oly Obst executive produce for 3 Arts Entertainment. Nanette Burstein will executive produce as well. Apple Studios will produce.

schema.headline: Amy Sedaris Joins Ben Stiller, Benicio Del Toro in Apple TV Comedy ‘Protective Custody’

title: Nicole Kidman Got Warned About Marrying Tom Cruise but Fired Back: ‘I Don’t Care. I’m in Love… Of Course I’ll Throw My Career Away’
description: Nicole Kidman said in a new British Vogue cover story that she was repeatedly warned about marrying Tom Cruise because it could hugely impact her ca
body:
Nicole Kidman said in a new British Vogue cover story that she was repeatedly warned about marrying Tom Cruise because it could hugely impact her career. The two A-listers met in 1989 during the production of Tony Scott’s “Days of Thunder,” which marked Kidman’s Hollywood feature debut. The duo got married one year later and stayed together for 11 years. Kidman credits the marriage and the immense tabloid scrutiny that followed with teaching her how to endure under the spotlight.
	

	“Strangely enough, I feel comfortable. Is that weird? That’s so weird,” Kidman said about life in the public eye. “But you have to remember literally, because of who I married at such a young age, I was thrust into it since I was 22… [My life has been] more time like that than not. My memory of it not being that is quite blurry, because I was really young.”


	“I got married so young,” Kidman continued about Cruise. “Suddenly I was 22, 23 years old and I had this huge movie star husband. But it just seemed completely natural. We just fell madly in love and it was that simple. I remember people saying to me, ‘OK, well this is really going to affect your career.’ I’m like, ‘I don’t care. I’m in love. I want to be married.’ And then I was his ‘wife’ and they were like, ‘See, we told you.’ I’m like, ‘So what? I wasn’t meant to marry the man I love? Of course I’ll throw my career away. I don’t care.’”

	While Kidman’s personal life became tabloid fodder during her decade married to Cruise, her film career took off with beloved titles such as “To Die For,” “The Portrait of a Lady” and “Practical Magic.” She made two movies with Cruise during their marriage: 1992’s misfire “Far and Away” and 1999’s classic “Eyes Wide Shut,” which marked the final movie of Stanley Kubrick’s career. 
	

	The couple announced their separation in February 2001, with Cruise filing for divorce that same month and citing irreconcilable differences. Kidman’s film career than exploded with the releases of “Moulin Rouge!” and “The Others” that year, followed by her Oscar-winning role in “The Hours” one year later.

	Kidman told Vanity Fair in 2013 that one of the main reasons her marriage to Cruise failed was because of just how young she was when the two got together. She explained: “I was a child, really, when I got married. And I needed to grow up.”

	Cruise recently mentioned Kidman in his Sight & Sound magazine interview earlier this year. According to Cruise, it was he who suggested casting Kidman to Kubrick for “Eyes Wide Shut.” Cruise wanted his wife to play the free-spirted Alice Harford opposite himself as the repressed New York socialite, Bill Harford.

	“I flew out to his house, and I landed in his backyard. I read the script the day before and we spent the day talking about it. I knew all of his films,” Cruise said. “Then it was basically he and I getting to know each other. And when we were doing that, I suggested Nicole play the role [of Alice]. Because, obviously, she’s a great actress.”

	Read Kidman’s full British Vogue cover story here.

schema.headline: Nicole Kidman Got Warned About Marrying Tom Cruise but Fired Back: ‘I Don’t Care. I’m in Love… Of Course I’ll Throw My Career Away’

title: Nicole Kidman, Elle Fanning Legal Drama Series ‘Discretion’ Casts Stephan James, Colton Ryan
description: Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning’s upcoming legal thriller series “Discretion” at Paramount+ is officially in production, with the series adding two n
body:
Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning’s upcoming legal thriller series “Discretion” at Paramount+ is officially in production, with the series adding two new cast members. 

	Both Stephan James (“I Play Rocky,” “If Beale Street Could Talk”) and Colton Ryan (“The Girl From Plainville,” Broadway’s “New York, New York”) are joining Kidman and Fanning in the show, alongside fellow cast member Josh Lucas. 


	The role marks a reunion for Fanning and Ryan, who previously starred together in the Hulu limited series “The Girl From Plainville.” 
	

	The logline for the show states that is “about summer associate Lenny (Fanning) at a prestigious Dallas law firm who uncovers a web of NDAs masking a dark truth. When she realizes she signed the same agreement, her discoveries put her in the crosshairs of the firm’s most powerful female partner Sharon (Kidman)—upending their mentor-protégé dynamic and raising the question: who gets to keep secrets, and at what cost.” 


	Both James and Ryan will appear in series regular roles. James will play Logan, described as “a sharp corporate associate who becomes a mentor to Lenny.” Ryan will play Boone, said to be “Lenny’s ex-boyfriend, a recovering addict from an affluent Dallas family, now nine months sober living at a halfway house while quietly trying to rebuild his life.” 

	James is repped by Gersh Agency, Range Media Partners, HillTop Entertainment, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman. Ryan is repped by Gersh and TFC Management. 

	“Discretion” is based on the short story of the same name by Chandler Baker. It has received an eight-episode order at Paramount+. 
	

	Baker is writing and executive producing, with both Kidman and Fanning executive producing in addition to starring. Susannah Grant is also attached to executive produce. Kidman is executive producing via Blossom Films with Per Saari, while Fanning, her sister Dakota Fanning, and Brittany Kahan Ward executive produce for Lewellen Pictures. Jordan Cerf of Linden Entertainment and Joe Hipps of Cut To will also executive produce. Matt Shakman will executive produce and direct the first four episodes. It will be produced by A24 for Paramount.

schema.headline: Nicole Kidman, Elle Fanning Legal Drama Series ‘Discretion’ Casts Stephan James, Colton Ryan

title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Casts Emily Hampshire,  Edvin Ryding, Robert Naylor, Sabrina Jalees, Priyanka
description:
“Heated Rivalry” is continuing to build out its Season 2 cast with five new additions. 

	Variety has learned that Emily Hampshire (“Schitt’s Creek,
body:
“Heated Rivalry” is continuing to build out its Season 2 cast with five new additions. 

	Variety has learned that Emily Hampshire (“Schitt’s Creek,” “VisionQuest”), Edvin Ryding (“The Young Royals,” “28 Years Later”), Robert Naylor (“Mile End Kicks,” “Cardinal”), Sabrina Jalees (“I Used to Be Funny,” “Black Mirror”), and Priyanka (“Drag Brunch Saved My Life,” “Meet Me Next Christmas”) are all joining the Crave-HBO Max series. 
	

	They will appear alongside returning stars Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie as well as fellow new additions Justice Smith and Charlie Gillespie. 


	The hit series is based on the “Game Changers” books by Rachel Reid. Hampshire will play Vanessa, with Ryding set to play Luca Haas. Naylor will play Wyatt Hayes, with Jalees as Farah Jalali. Priyanka will play Tarek. 

	Hampshire is repped by Atlas Artists, Paradigm, Creative Drive Artists and Felker, McGinnis & Ryan. Ryding is repped by CAA, Agentfirman Planthaber/Kildén/Mandic/ Boström, and Independent Talent Group. Naylor is repped by Agence M. Jalees is repped by WME and OPE Partners. Priyanka is repped by The Talent House. 

	“Heated Rivalry” became the surprise hit of 2025, with the show rapidly becoming a major cultural phenomenon when it launched in November of that year despite little promotion. It was renewed for a second season in December. 

	The official logline for Season 1 states, “Rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie) are bound by ambition, rivalry, and a magnetic pull neither of them fully understood. What began as a secret fling between two fresh-faced rookies evolved into a years-long journey of love, denial, and self-discovery.” 
	

	The series is commissioned by Bell Media’s Crave with the participation of the Canada Media Fund (CMF). Jacob Tierney serves as writer, director, and executive producer. Brendan Brady and Jayme Alter Wilson also executive produce. Lori Fischburg and Liane Cunje are producers, with Reid as consulting producer. Mike Goldbach serves as co-writer on Season 2. The series is distributed internationally by Sphere Abacus, a Bell Media company.

schema.headline: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Casts Emily Hampshire,  Edvin Ryding, Robert Naylor, Sabrina Jalees, Priyanka

title: Yash’s ‘Toxic’ Gets a Sonic Fairy Tale From Composer Vishal Mishra: ‘I Understand the Language of Love’
description:
Vishal Mishra keeps coming back to one word: honest. 

	Ask him about competing with streaming playlists, about his string of Bollywood hits, about
body:
Vishal Mishra keeps coming back to one word: honest. 

	Ask him about competing with streaming playlists, about his string of Bollywood hits, about writing a love song for a film soaked in violence, and the composer-singer circles back to the same idea: the music has to be true to the moment it was born from, or it isn’t worth making.

	That instinct is on full display in “Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups,” Geetu Mohandas‘ gangster saga starring Yash, which arrives in theaters worldwide on Aug. 26. Mishra composed four of the soundtrack’s six songs, sharing the album with Ravi Basrur, Tanishk Bagchi and Faheem Abdullah. It’s his first collaboration with Mohandas and Yash, and he describes it as the product of a creative partnership built on trust rather than a scorecard of credits.
	

	“It does mark my first collaboration with Geetu and Yash bhai, and honestly, it’s not even about the number of songs,” Mishra tells Variety. “It’s about this journey we have been on for such a long time, and I am so glad that I have met collaborators who get the best out of me.”


	The clearest example of that trust is “Tabaahi,” the first song released from the film and, by Mishra’s account, its emotional thesis statement. Written by Raj Shekhar with Mishra composing and singing, the track had to announce an entire cinematic world before audiences had seen a frame of the movie.

	He describes it as a song about destruction dressed up as a love song, or perhaps the other way around. The scale of two people colliding, he says, mirrors the scale of the world Mohandas built on screen, and the production followed her lead instrument by instrument.
	

	“Every beat, every instrument is synced to the frame of the visuals, which is magical,” Mishra says. “And I am just very happy to be a part of this magic.”

	Mishra pushes back on the idea that romance and darkness sit at odds with each other in “Toxic.” He argues the opposite is often true, that some of the deepest love plays out in the bleakest settings, and that shaped how “Tabaahi” was built. The melody, he says, carries the heart of the song while the production carries its tension, with Mohandas and Yash giving him room to avoid anything that felt like a conventional love theme.

	That same appetite for the unfamiliar drove “Waqt,” which folds an EDM and dubstep-leaning production into a traditionally romantic Hindi film melody, including an English verse. Mishra credits the film’s visual language for demanding a hybrid rather than a straightforward ballad, and singles out Yash as a creative partner who gave him the space to work through the idea slowly.

	“You find magic in the spaces where nothing exists,” Mishra says. “I always believe in leaving that space, and you know, Yash bhai, I found a brother in him.”

	“Toxic” also leans into the multilingual sprawl of the Indian market, releasing its songs across five languages, with the English-language “Peekaboo” pulling in collaborators from Los Angeles as well as Mumbai. Mishra estimates more than 150 people worked across the album’s various versions. Rounding out the soundtrack are “Madhosh,” composed by Bagchi, Arslan Nizami and Abdullah with vocals from Siddharth Basrur; “Chingariyaan,” sung by Jonita Gandhi; and “His Aura Hits You,” composed by Ravi Basrur with Mishra on vocals. The music is released by Zee Music Company.

	Mishra arrives at “Toxic” on the back of a run that has made him one of Bollywood’s most in-demand melody writers, anchored by last year’s “Saiyaara,” whose soundtrack included the Mishra-composed “Tum Ho Toh,” written by Raj Shekhar and sung by Mishra alongside Hansika Pareek. That success builds on two earlier career peaks: “Kaise Hua,” from “Kabir Singh” in 2019, and “Pehle Bhi Main,” from “Animal” in 2023, both of which were among the biggest Hindi film songs of their respective years. He waves off the idea that hits like those create pressure.

	“I really don’t think about numbers,” he says. “I feel they’re vaguely overrated and I really don’t understand that. I understand the language of love, and that’s what I believe in.”
	

	He traces his real turning point back to “Kaise Hua,” the song he says first pulled together threads he had been composing across languages for years. Since then, his catalog has spanned the country. He says every language that belongs to India matters equally to him, and that the goal has never been about language but about reaching as many people as possible.

	Looking past “Toxic,” Mishra says he is scoring his first Telugu-language film, with Vijay Deverakonda attached, alongside upcoming projects with Salman Khan, Ahaan Pandey, Sandeep Reddy Vanga and Mohit Suri, plus a slate with production banner Cine1. 

	“The urge of creation right now that I have has never been there like this,” he says. “I hope that I get to create even more, and I hope that I get to touch more souls and touch my fans who are like my family, in a way that it becomes a memory.”

schema.headline: Yash’s ‘Toxic’ Gets a Sonic Fairy Tale From Composer Vishal Mishra: ‘I Understand the Language of Love’

title: A Bulldog in Business: How Moving into the Booth Opened Other Doors for Dodger Great Orel Hershiser
description: Orel Hershiser knows that he is a bona fide Los Angeles icon. But he has no illusions — he wouldn’t have the business opportunities he enjoys today
body:
Orel Hershiser knows that he is a bona fide Los Angeles icon. But he has no illusions — he wouldn’t have the business opportunities he enjoys today without the platform provided by his broadcasting gig with the team.

	“You have a resume, but the resume slowly dies,” Hershiser says. “You have to be active. You have to be pertinent. I always have wanted to be introduced as ‘He is,’ not ‘He was.’ ‘He is’ is really important to me.”
	

	Despite his busy travel schedule during baseball season, Hershiser is hands-on in running his businesses. For this interview, he donned a slate-gray polo shirt embossed with the rectangular Chevrolet logo and arranged for the sit-down to take place amid the Corvettes on display on the showroom floor of the Chino auto dealership that was reopened with Hershiser’s imprimatur in May.Hershiser has been energized by the challenge of learning an entirely new sector with his move into automotive. 


	RELATED STORY: Dodger Great Orel Hershiser on the Devotion to Broadcasting, Baseball and Faith That Led Him to the Hollywood Walk of Fame

	As he was in baseball, Hershiser is a quick study and doesn’t miss an opportunity to promote his latest brand.

	“We are conveniently located off the 60 freeway at Central and Riverside, and we would love to see you,” Hershiser enthuses before the interview wraps.

	Hershiser’s other public-facing business is the Legends Attic sports memorabilia shop in Claremont, which opened in 2024. It is partly a museum-style showcase of Hershiser’s career kudos and mementos as well collectable items for sale from other icons in from a range of other sports and cities.
	

	“We speak on a daily basis,” says Eddie Allizadeh, who is Hershiser’s business partner.

	Allizadeh initially reached out to Hershiser about five years ago with an offer for him to appear at his sports collectibles shop in Victorville.

	“He said no to us to do an appearance. He was more interested in doing business ventures,” Allizadeh says. “I asked for a few moments of his time to do lunch in Pasadena and the story goes from there.”

	Hershiser invested in Allizadeh’s automotive sales representation firm Lane4 before the two teamed to buy out the long-established auto shop M.K. Smith Chevrolet in Chino. When the sale was announced, Hershiser arranged with Chino officials to appear as a surprise guest at Mayor Eunice Ulloa’s state of the city address in April.

	“Hello Chino! Hello Dodger fans! Oh my gosh,” Hershiser told the crowd as he bounded out on stage wearing a Dodger blue blazer with the team’s logo.

	“What you saw from me on the baseball field — I’m going to bring that here,” Hershiser enthused.

schema.headline: A Bulldog in Business: How Moving into the Booth Opened Other Doors for Dodger Great Orel Hershiser

title: Viu, TrueVisions Now Launch Content Collaboration in Southeast Asia
description: Viu and TrueVisions Now are launching a content collaboration that brings a curated slate of premium Thai series to Viu users across Southeast Asia,
body:
Viu and TrueVisions Now are launching a content collaboration that brings a curated slate of premium Thai series to Viu users across Southeast Asia, with a branded zone debuting Aug. 20 in Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

	The zone opens with six series pulled from TrueVisions Now’s catalogue, with the roster expected to expand in subsequent phases. Viewers can reach the new zone through either of Viu’s viewing options, the ad-supported free tier or the paid subscription tier, across the app’s supported devices.
	

	For TrueVisions Now, the tie-up represents its first move into regional content distribution outside its home market, with both companies pointing to a shared push to widen access to quality entertainment from across Asia. The pairing lets Viu’s footprint across Southeast Asia carry TrueVisions Now’s expanding library to new audiences in the region.


	The branded zone will launch with six series. They include the comedy “A Sample Family,” starring Puak Pongsathorn Jongwilas, Cris Horwang and Neen Neenara Boonnithipaisit, in which a struggling family secretly settles into a lavish show house and fabricates a picture of online perfection to help their daughter land a spot at an international school; the rom-com “Oops! I’m the Concubine,” starring Emma Panisara Yang and Peterpan Tadsapon Wiwitawan, about a modern woman transported to an earlier era who must learn to adapt rather than resist her new circumstances; and the rom-com “My Wife’s Gunslinger God,” starring Aom Sushar Manaying and Mew Suppasit Jongcheveevat, following a secretive gamer who agrees to a yearlong marriage of convenience with her first love, aiming to win him over before time runs out.
	

	Also included are the comedy “The Cops Spy on Stage,” starring Nichamon Kham-in, Atchariya Sritha and Somchai Saiutha, centered on a young police officer who assembles a makeshift squad to revisit a case connected to his father’s history, turning the covert assignment into a blend of comedy and danger; the horror-drama “Mui Fei The Medium,” starring Pat Chayanit Chansangavej and Offroad Kantapon Jindataweepol, about a young medium who returns as a vengeful spirit after surviving human trafficking; and the romance “To Love and Cherish,” starring Film Thanapat Kawila and Bua Nalinthip Sakulongampai, about a woman who reunites with her first love years after losing touch.

	Viu operates across markets in Asia, the Middle East and South Africa under PCCW Media. TrueVisions Now positions itself as Thailand’s all-in-one platform for sports and entertainment, bringing together streaming partners including Viu, iQIYI and WeTV under its “Nowtainment” concept.

	Janice Lee, CEO of PCCW Media Group and Viu, said: “Thai content continues to resonate with viewers across the region, and we are pleased to collaborate with TrueVisions Now to bring more premium series to Viu. The addition strengthens our content offering while expanding opportunities for audiences to discover quality entertainment from across Asia.”

	Ongard Prapakamol, head of TrueVisions and media at True Corporation Plc, said the collaboration marked an important step in expanding the reach of the company’s content beyond Thailand. “Through Viu’s regional platform, we look forward to introducing our series to new viewers in Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines,” he said. “It also highlights the growing influence of Thai creative talent and culture across the region.”

schema.headline: Viu, TrueVisions Now Launch Content Collaboration in Southeast Asia

title: Ken Russell’s Controversial NC-17 Horror Film ‘The Devils’ Sets First Look at Restored Cut – Film News in Brief
description:
Ken Russell‘s controversial film “The Devils” will finally be seen in its original form, as seen in a new trailer for the NC-17 release.

	The 4K re
body:
Ken Russell‘s controversial film “The Devils” will finally be seen in its original form, as seen in a new trailer for the NC-17 release.

	The 4K restoration references Russell’s private edit from 2004 and serves as the first release from Warner Bros. Clockwork, the studio’s new specialty label. The British horror film stars Oscar-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, telling the story of Urbain Grandier, a 17th-century priest who was accused of witchcraft.
	

	“The Devils” was originally released in 1971 and, at the time, recieved an X rating for its highly violent and sexual content. This restored cut, which world premiered at this year’s Cannes Film Festival, will finally show Russell’s original vision. It is set to play at the Toronto International Film Festival in September.


	Russell also directed “Altered States,” “Women in Love” and “Tommy.”

	“The Devils” releases in the U.S. on Oct. 16 for an exclusive, one-week engagement with select 35mm screenings. Watch the trailer below.


	
		Tuesday, August 11	
	
		Studio Ghibli Fest 2026 Continues With Hayao Miyazaki’s ‘Castle in the Sky’	

	Tickets are on sale now for Hayao Miyazaki’s “Castle in the Sky.” 

	The film, which follows Pazu and Sheeta on their search for the legendary floating castle and the mystery of the luminous crystal, returns to theaters for its 40th anniversary as part of Studio Ghibli Fest. The seven-title lineup also features the 25th anniversary of “Spirited Away.”

	“Castle in the Sky” will be shown in both the original Japanese and English-dubbed versions, with the voices of Anna Paquin, James Van Der Beek, Cloris Leachman, Mark Hamill and Mandy Patinkin. Screenings will also include a post-film clip from the featurette “The World of Laputa.”
	

	The Studio Ghibli film’s theatrical run is Aug. 22-26.
	
		Robert Patrick Joins Psychological Thriller ‘Outpost: LMS’	

	Robert Patrick will star in “Outpost: LMS,” the sophomore feature from writer and director Brad Courtemanche.

	Patrick joins the psychological thriller as the voice of the mysterious Commanding Officer, alongside Omar Moustafa Ghonim and Sheree Abate. The film follows a grieving mother who accidentally shoots a reclusive soldier in the Vermont wilderness and becomes trapped in his outpost.

	The film will enter production this November in Vermont as production company GrizzlieBradFilms LLC eyes a 2028 debut.

	Courtemanche’s debut feature, “What Only Cicadas See,” is awaiting its festival premiere.

                            6:03 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            A Texas high school teacher broke down in tears on video while describing his students' lack of education after they couldn't complete a reading and writing task.
      
    
            Darius Williams, a teacher at Wheatley High School in Houston, posted the video on Instagram after he completed a three-hour class with seniors who are about to go off to college next year.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In the clip, Williams starts weeping because he says his students cannot read or write -- even when he gives them help to complete the assignments.
      

            He said he provided the seniors with two paragraphs to read and then asked them to write just one sentence -- but claims they couldn't accomplish the easy exercise.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As a result, Williams was crushed emotionally ... and the video shows every moment of his pain, knowing that his students -- almost all of them young Black men and women -- are leaving high school with no real education.
      
    
            Check out the video ... it's worth the watch.

title: Travis Barker Says Life Felt Like 'Final Destination' After Surviving Plane Crash
description:
Travis Barker
                          Plane Crash Made My Life Feel Like 'Final Destination'
body:
Travis Barker
                          Plane Crash Made My Life Feel Like 'Final Destination'
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 13, 2026
                            9:06 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Travis Barker felt like he was trapped in his own personal horror film after he survived a plane crash ... and he believed death would catch up to him like in "Final Destination."
      
    
            Here's the deal ... back in 2008, Travis and his friend Adam "DJ AM" Goldstein survived a plane crash which killed 4 other people. The following year, Goldstein died from a drug overdose -- which is when Travis began to really struggle with his trauma.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Travis tells People he felt like -- given what had happened -- he was living in "Final Destination" ... and he feared going out because he worried he'd end up dead.
      

            He says, "I would go from my tour bus to the hotel, and no one would see me. I would just hide out. I was so afraid. I was just waiting for impact in the bus. I was just like, 'Oh, I'm next. I'm going to go anytime.'"
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Travis says there's no way to prepare for a friend dying suddenly ... especially after surviving a plane crash together ... but he ultimately had to accept that his friends would want him to live his life instead of fearing what might happen.
      
    
            His assistant, bodyguard and the plane's two pilots died in the crash ... and it took years for Travis to start flying again.
      
    
            Travis has a new documentary, "Louder Than Fear," dropping today on Hulu and Disney+ ... and he's sure to talk about this and a whole lot more.
